bib.title: Failure as a Process: An Anatomy of CLI Coding Agent Trajectories

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Failure as a Process: An Anatomy of CLI Coding Agent Trajectories", Xiangxin Zhao*, Han Li*, Shuaiting Li, Tianyi Zhao, Earl T. Barr, Federica Sarro, He Ye. Preprint: the only venue marking printed is "arXiv:2607.09510v1 [cs.SE] 10 Jul 2026" (IEEE-style layout, no conference named). Affiliations as printed: Zhao (first author) "University College London, London, United Kingdom"; co-first Han Li "Nanjing University, Nanjing, China".

COVERAGE: 12 of 12 pages, 66,860 of 66,860 chars. Pages 1-10 are the body, 11-12 are references (skimmed). There are no appendices. All six figure captions were read; plotted values in Figs 2 and 4 were read from extracted text only.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- claim: The decisive error comes early, around a quarter of the way into a failed run.
  number: median step 7 (mean 11.92); failed runs median 27 steps (mean 42)
  setup: 1,184 failed trajectories, Terminal-Bench, 89 tasks, 3 scaffolds x 7 models; t_err labelled in hindsight
  quote: "failed runs contain a median of 27 execution steps (mean 42), whereas the median decisive error occurs at only step 7 (mean 11.92)"
  where: p5

- claim: Failure is modelled with three timestamps: t_err (decisive error), t_lock (no correct recovery observed afterwards), t_obs (first observable sign). Two measures are derived from them: fix window = t_lock − t_err, observability lag = t_obs − t_lock.
  number: medians 7 / 12 / 16; means 11.9 / 18.6 / 22.5
  setup: same 1,184 runs; t_obs statistics cover only the runs that surface
  quote: "terr median 7, mean 11.9 / tlock median 12, mean 18.6 / tobs median 16, mean 22.5 (of the 72% that surface)"
  where: p5, Fig. 4

- claim: The visible signal trails the decisive error by about ten steps, and 28% of failures never surface.
  number: about 10 steps; 28% silent
  setup: difference of medians across runs, not a per-run median gap
  quote: "the median first observable failure (tobs) occurs at approximately step 16, around ten execution steps after the median decisive error (step 7)"; "72% ceiling 28% of failures NEVER surface (silent)"
  where: p5

- claim: The fix window is short.
  number: median 1 step; 60.9% have at least 1; 43.9% have 3 or more; 239 runs have more than 10
  setup: same 1,184 runs
  quote: "The median recovery window (t lock −t err) is one execution steps, with 60.9% of decisive errors leaving at least one recovery step, 43.9% leaving three or more, and 239 trajectories remaining recoverable for over ten steps."
  where: p5

- claim: Most successful runs also contain an error and recover from it. What separates them from failed runs is acting on the signal.
  number: 71% of successes recover from at least one error; 92% vs 37% respond to a signal; signals arrive at 74% vs 72%; recovery length median 5 vs 12 steps
  setup: 610 successful vs 1,184 failed runs
  quote: "71% of successful trajectories encounter at least one error before eventually succeeding"; "92% of successful trajectories respond to at least one error signal, compared with only 37% of failed trajectories"; "Successful recoveries are much shorter than failed ones (median 5 vs. 12 execution steps)."
  where: p8-9

- claim: Labels are LLM-drafted and human-finalised, with double annotation.
  number: Cohen's κ 0.78-0.94; κ = 0.83 for root causes; weighted κ ≥ 0.94 for timepoints
  setup: Claude Opus 4.6 writes the draft; two of four annotators review every failed trajectory; disagreements resolved by discussion
  quote: "independent annotation by two of four annotators for every failed trajectory, and high inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's κ= 0.83 for root causes and weighted κ≥0.94 for the three timepoints)"
  where: p10 (also p4)

- claim: An outcome-blind prefix monitor confirms failures but rarely anticipates them.
  number: 82% precision; recall 18.2% rising to 28.8% when given the task requirements; median lead time 0; 3.7-8.7% flagged before lock-in; false-positive rate 2-3%
  setup: Claude Sonnet 4.6; 2,659 prefixes from 600 trajectories (300 failed, 300 successful)
  quote: "flagging locked-in runs at 82% precision, but it lacks foresight: its median lead time relative tot lock is zero, only 3.7–8.7% of failures are flagged before lock-in"
  where: p6

- claim: Root causes are mostly epistemic.
  number: epistemic 57.9%, competence 32.8%, environment 9.4%; false premise 30.7%; epistemic share per system 44-80%
  setup: trigger at t_err, 1,184 runs
  quote: "epistemic triggers account for 57.9% of all decisive errors, substantially exceeding competence (32.8%) and environment (9.4%)"
  where: p7, Tables II and V

- claim: After lock-in most runs keep going, and 26% fabricate success.
  number: 18% stop immediately; "repairs the wrong problem" is 24% of runs but 39% of wasted steps (median tail 21); fabrication in 26%, with 84% of it starting at or after lock-in
  setup: failed runs, dominant-behaviour labelling by a first-match rule
  quote: "Fabricated success, where the agent claims results or completion with fake evidence, appears in 26% of failed trajectories."
  where: p8-9, Table III

- claim: Pass rates across the 21 systems.
  number: 19% to 45%
  setup: 89 aligned tasks
  quote: "pass rates ranging from 19% to 45% across the 21 coding agent systems"
  where: p9, Table IV

LIMITS
- No confidence intervals, standard errors or significance tests anywhere. Every figure is a point estimate.
- No repeated runs: each task-system pair appears to have one trajectory, so run-to-run variance is not measured.
- "Unrecoverable" is empirical only, which the authors concede: "we did not observe the agent recovering from these errors, not that we know that it is impossible".
- t_err is the decisive error labelled in hindsight, "not necessarily the first error to appear". The paper therefore does not measure distance from the first error.
- The "about 10 steps" gap is a difference of medians. No per-run distribution of t_obs − t_err is given, and the median fix window of 1 does not equal the gap between the t_lock and t_err medians (5).
- Both annotators reviewed the same Opus draft, so κ may be inflated by anchoring. This is not discussed, and no agreement between the LLM draft and the final labels is reported.
- Which label scored κ = 0.78 is not stated. Agreement is stated only for failed trajectories; the labels behind the 71% and 92% figures for successful runs have no stated agreement.
- Selection: 3,843 of a theoretical 5,040 runs completed, and only the 89 of 240 tasks with all 21 systems were kept. Timeouts and abnormal terminations are excluded, a bias the authors concede. 71.4% of the data is reused from prior work [29].
- One benchmark (Terminal-Bench). Cross-system comparisons are "observational rather than causal".
- The "median 5 vs 12" recovery length is not precisely defined for the failed side.
- Dated: the models are Claude Sonnet 4, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Qwen3 Coder 480B, DeepSeek V3.2, Kimi K2, Devstral 2, with runs "from May 2025 onward".

BUILDS ON: Terminal-Bench (Merrill et al., 2026) [19]; reused trajectories from CodeTracer (Li et al., 2026) [29]; the prefix monitor is adapted from log-based anomaly detection (Zhang et al., 2019) [32]; the definition of a step from ReAct (Yao et al., 2023) [20]; LLM-judge caution from Crupi et al., 2025 [31]. It positions itself against Bouzenia and Pradel 2025, MAST (Cemri et al., 2025), Who&When (Zhang et al., 2025), AgentLens (Sahoo et al., 2026) and Mehtiyev and Assunção 2026.

CODE: none in the paper. Dataset, codebook and prompts are said to be at https://github.com/xz-Sean/cli trajectory analysis.git (the URL extracted with spaces, probably underscores; I did not check it).

FIGURES: one candidate, Fig. 4, p5: "Distributions of the three annotated failure timestamps across 1,184 failed trajectories." Three cumulative curves show the 7 / 12 / 16 medians and the 72% ceiling for t_obs in one picture, which makes the onset, lock-in and visibility gaps plus the silent 28% readable at a glance. Fig. 3 (p4) is the schematic alternative if a definition diagram is preferred.

PROBLEMS: Extraction is clean apart from dropped spaces around italics ("tot lock", "explainwhatwent") and figure text interleaved with body text on pages 3-6. No embedded instructions in the PDF. Internal inconsistency in the source: environment is given as 9.4% but includes "Other" at 0.6% (8.8 + 0.6). Fabrication is 15% as a dominant behaviour and 26% by occurrence; both are correct under their own definitions.
